terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 1: AI fundamentals and literacy (24%) / Foundations and terminology

terms.definition: A layered model loosely inspired by the brain. Exam angle: Background only. You won't be asked how it works.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 1: AI fundamentals and literacy (24%) / Foundations and terminology

terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 1: AI fundamentals and literacy (24%) / Foundations and terminology

terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 1: AI fundamentals and literacy (24%) / Foundations and terminology

terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 1: AI fundamentals and literacy (24%) / Foundations and terminology

terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 1: AI fundamentals and literacy (24%) / Foundations and terminology

terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 1: AI fundamentals and literacy (24%) / Foundations and terminology

terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 1: AI fundamentals and literacy (24%) / Foundations and terminology

terms.definition: End result (revenue, cost savings). Exam angle: Proves value, but slowly.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Share of target users actively using the tool. Exam angle: No adoption, no value.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: (Benefit − cost) ÷ cost. Exam angle: Includes people, data and change costs, not just licenses.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Time until benefits cover costs. Exam angle: Executives often ask for this.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Value of future cash flows in today's money. Exam angle: Awareness level.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Costs prevented (for example, hires not needed). Exam angle: A soft saving. Label it honestly.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Cash savings vs time or capacity freed. Exam angle: Freed time is only valuable if it's redeployed.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: More output per person or hour. Exam angle: Common generative AI value claim. Measure against the baseline.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Cost of each AI-handled unit (call, document, query). Exam angle: A unit-economics view.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Cost and value per unit of work. Exam angle: Check that it still works at scale.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Comparing AI vs non-AI groups. Exam angle: The cleanest way to attribute impact.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Proving AI caused the improvement. Exam angle: Use control groups and baselines.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Actually capturing the benefits promised. Exam angle: Needs process change, not just deployment.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Benefits that are hard to count (experience, brand, employee satisfaction). Exam angle: Real, but state them separately from ROI.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Business value, KPIs and ROI

terms.definition: Pay per use, for example per token or request. Exam angle: Good for variable or uncertain demand.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Pay-as-you-go model calls. Exam angle: Flexible. No commitment.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Reserved model capacity for a commitment. Exam angle: Predictable, high, steady volume.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Processing many requests together, not in real time. Exam angle: Lower cost when results aren't urgent.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Pay for compute instances by time. Exam angle: Custom models, steady workloads.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Fixed price per user per month. Exam angle: Predictable. Typical for assistants and SaaS.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Discount for committing to steady usage. Exam angle: For predictable baselines.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Practices for managing cloud cost with shared accountability. Exam angle: Track AI spend by use case.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Tokens in and out, model size, call volume, context length, RAG storage. Exam angle: Smaller models and shorter prompts cut cost.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Picking the smallest model that meets quality needs. Exam angle: A major cost lever.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: Data prep, integration, change management, monitoring, people. Exam angle: Often exceed the model cost.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / AI cost models

terms.definition: An edge competitors can't easily copy. Exam angle: Proprietary data and workflows, not the model itself.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Competitive advantage and transformation

terms.definition: Unique data that makes your AI better. Exam angle: The model is a commodity. Your data isn't.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Competitive advantage and transformation

terms.definition: Lead the market vs adopt proven approaches. Exam angle: Fast-following is lower risk for non-core uses.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Competitive advantage and transformation

terms.definition: How customers perceive interactions. Exam angle: Personalization, faster service.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Competitive advantage and transformation

terms.definition: Doing the same with less cost or time. Exam angle: The most common early AI value.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Competitive advantage and transformation

terms.definition: New products, services or revenue streams built on AI. Exam angle: Highest value, highest uncertainty.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Competitive advantage and transformation

terms.definition: Rethinking processes with technology. Exam angle: AI is a layer on top of it, not a replacement.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Competitive advantage and transformation

terms.definition: Changing workflows to fit AI. Exam angle: Bolting AI onto a broken process limits value.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 2: AI strategy and business value (28%) / Competitive advantage and transformation

terms.definition: Designing and using AI that is safe, fair and trustworthy. Exam angle: AWS frames it as eight dimensions (the next eight rows).
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Outcomes don't unfairly disadvantage groups. Exam angle: Test outcomes across demographic groups.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Understanding why the AI produced an output. Exam angle: Required for regulated decisions.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Protecting data and the model from misuse. Exam angle: Least privilege, encryption, data minimization.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Preventing harmful outputs and misuse. Exam angle: Content filters, guardrails.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Ability to monitor and steer AI behavior. Exam angle: Override, shut-off and human control.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Correct outputs, even with unexpected or adversarial inputs. Exam angle: Grounding, testing, red-teaming.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Defined processes and accountability for AI. Exam angle: Covers the whole AI lifecycle.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Being open about when and how AI is used. Exam angle: Disclose AI interactions to customers.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: A named person or team owns AI outcomes. Exam angle: "The model did it" is never an answer.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Considering diverse users and impacts. Exam angle: Diverse teams and test data.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Tensions such as accuracy vs explainability or personalization vs privacy. Exam angle: Decide them explicitly, document them, and match them to risk.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Responsible AI principles

terms.definition: Policies, roles and processes for approving and overseeing AI. Exam angle: Enables safe speed. It isn't a blocker.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Building controls in from the start. Exam angle: Beats bolting them on after launch.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Cross-functional decision body. Exam angle: Legal, risk, security, business, data and HR together.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Shared ownership across departments. Exam angle: IT alone can't govern AI.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Organization-wide rules for AI use. Exam angle: Acceptable use, data handling, approvals.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: A catalog of all AI systems in use. Exam angle: You can't govern what you can't see. It counters shadow AI.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Documentation of a model's intended use, limits and performance. Exam angle: Transparency. AWS publishes AI Service Cards.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Evaluating potential harms before deployment. Exam angle: Required for higher-risk uses.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: A record of decisions, data, versions and approvals. Exam angle: Supports regulators and investigations.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Oversight from idea through retirement. Exam angle: Includes monitoring and decommissioning.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed. Exam angle: Clarifies who owns what.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Business owns risk, risk/compliance oversees, audit checks. Exam angle: A familiar risk-management model.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Governance and accountability

terms.definition: Meeting laws that apply to AI and data. Exam angle: Involve legal early.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: EU law that classifies AI by risk (unacceptable, high, limited, minimal). Exam angle: The model for risk-tiered governance.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: EU data protection law. Exam angle: Lawful basis, data minimization, rights over automated decisions.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Where data is physically stored. Exam angle: Choose Regions accordingly.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Which country's laws govern the data. Exam angle: Different from residency.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Personally identifiable information. Exam angle: Mask or redact before sending to models.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Using only the data that's needed. Exam angle: Reduces privacy risk.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Permission to use personal data for a purpose. Exam angle: Reusing data for AI may need new consent.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Who can use which data and models. Exam angle: Least privilege, role-based access.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Minimum access needed to do the job. Exam angle: Applies to AI agents too.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Protecting data at rest and in transit. Exam angle: A baseline expectation.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Labeling data by sensitivity. Exam angle: Decides what can go into which AI tool.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Sensitive data exposed through AI tools or prompts. Exam angle: A shadow AI risk.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: AWS secures the cloud and its services; the customer secures its data, access, prompts and use. Exam angle: A frequent exam topic.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: US framework: Govern, Map, Measure, Manage. Exam angle: Awareness of a common framework.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: International standard for AI management systems. Exam angle: A certifiable AI governance standard.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Regulatory and compliance

terms.definition: Tiering AI uses by potential harm. Exam angle: Controls scale with the tier.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Affects rights, safety, money or access (hiring, credit, health). Exam angle: Needs human oversight, testing and documentation.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Systematic unfairness in data or outputs. Exam angle: Comes from historical data. Test and monitor for it.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Past discrimination reflected in training data. Exam angle: Example: a hiring model that favors past hires.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Training data doesn't represent all users. Exam angle: Example: face recognition that works worse for some groups.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Fabricated but confident output. Exam angle: Mitigate with RAG, grounding, citations and human review.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Offensive, dangerous or inappropriate outputs. Exam angle: Content filters and guardrails.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Outputs that infringe copyright, or leaks of your own IP. Exam angle: Check vendor indemnity and keep confidential data out.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Vendor protection against IP claims on outputs. Exam angle: A buy-side consideration.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Malicious input that hijacks model instructions. Exam angle: Especially dangerous for agents with tools.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Tricking a model into ignoring its safety rules. Exam angle: Guardrails plus monitoring.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Corrupting training data to change behavior. Exam angle: Secure the data pipeline.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Silent performance decay. Exam angle: Monitoring is a governance duty.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: People trusting AI output without checking. Exam angle: Training and review steps.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Brand damage from AI failures. Exam angle: Often the biggest real-world cost.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Deliberately attacking AI to find weaknesses. Exam angle: Do it before launch for public-facing generative AI.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: Log of AI risks, owners and mitigations. Exam angle: Living document.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / AI risk management

terms.definition: A person approves before the output takes effect. Exam angle: High-risk decisions.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Human oversight and safeguards

terms.definition: A person monitors and can intervene. Exam angle: Medium-risk automation.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Human oversight and safeguards

terms.definition: Fully automated. Exam angle: Only for low-risk, well-tested uses.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Human oversight and safeguards

terms.definition: Route to a human when AI is unsure or the topic is sensitive. Exam angle: Confidence thresholds trigger it.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Human oversight and safeguards

terms.definition: Controls that filter or block unwanted inputs and outputs. Exam angle: Topics, PII, toxicity, grounding checks.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Human oversight and safeguards

terms.definition: Blocking harmful categories of content. Exam angle: Part of guardrails.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Human oversight and safeguards

terms.definition: Ability to quickly stop or revert AI. Exam angle: A controllability requirement.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Human oversight and safeguards

terms.definition: Telling users they're interacting with AI. Exam angle: Builds trust. Sometimes legally required.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Human oversight and safeguards

terms.definition: Spot-checking a share of outputs. Exam angle: Ongoing quality assurance.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 3: Governance and responsible AI (24%) / Human oversight and safeguards

terms.definition: Evaluating preparedness across strategy, people, process, data, technology, culture and governance. Exam angle: Do it before big investments.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Readiness and maturity

terms.definition: Stages from experimenting to AI-driven. Exam angle: Typical stages: exploring → piloting → operationalizing → scaling → transforming.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Readiness and maturity

terms.definition: Difference between current and needed skills or tools. Exam angle: Close it by hiring, training or partnering.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Readiness and maturity

terms.definition: Comparing current state with target state. Exam angle: Feeds the roadmap.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Readiness and maturity

terms.definition: Sequenced plan of initiatives and enablers. Exam angle: Quick wins first, foundations in parallel.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Readiness and maturity

terms.definition: Where you are vs where you want to be. Exam angle: Classic change-planning framing.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Readiness and maturity

terms.definition: Attitudes toward experimentation, data and risk. Exam angle: Culture is often the real blocker.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Readiness and maturity

terms.definition: Data is available, accurate, accessible, governed and labeled where needed. Exam angle: Usually the number one blocker to AI value.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: Data trapped in one department or system. Exam angle: Breaking silos often comes before AI.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: A named owner accountable for a data set. Exam angle: Needed for quality and access decisions.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: Person who maintains data quality day to day. Exam angle: Operational data role.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: Policies for data quality, access, lineage and use. Exam angle: A foundation for AI governance.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: Where data came from and how it changed. Exam angle: Auditability and trust.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: Searchable inventory of data assets. Exam angle: Helps teams find and trust data.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: Central store for raw data of any type. Exam angle: A common AI data foundation on AWS (Amazon S3).
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: Automated flow moving and transforming data. Exam angle: Keeps AI inputs fresh.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: One trusted version of key data. Exam angle: Reduces conflicting outputs.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: Cloud resources that grow with demand. Exam angle: Avoids rebuilding for scale.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Data and infrastructure foundations

terms.definition: Structured approach to moving people to new ways of working. Exam angle: Plan it from day one, not at launch.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Senior leader who champions and funds the initiative. Exam angle: Strongest predictor of success. Removes roadblocks.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Getting affected groups to agree on goals. Exam angle: Do it early and keep doing it.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Pushback from fear, habit or job-loss worries. Exam angle: Address it with transparency, involvement and reskilling.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Basic understanding of AI across the workforce. Exam angle: Everyone needs some. Builders need depth.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Building new skills for the current role. Exam angle: AI literacy, prompting.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Training people for different roles. Exam angle: For roles AI changes the most.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Systematic investment in skills. Exam angle: Role-based learning paths.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Moving people from doing tasks to reviewing, judging and handling exceptions. Exam angle: Augmentation framing reduces fear.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Enthusiasts embedded in teams who drive adoption. Exam angle: Peer influence beats mandates.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Who hears what, when and why. Exam angle: Transparency builds trust.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Freedom to experiment and admit mistakes. Exam angle: Enables learning with AI.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Business, data, technical, legal and risk working together. Exam angle: Default team model for AI initiatives.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Business person accountable for the AI product's value. Exam angle: Keeps work tied to outcomes.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement. Exam angle: A common change model, at awareness level.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Change management and workforce

terms.definition: Moving from pilot to enterprise-wide use. Exam angle: Needs repeatable processes, platforms and governance.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Scaling AI

terms.definition: Deploying in stages by team, region or use case. Exam angle: Limits risk and lets you learn.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Scaling AI

terms.definition: Small cycles of build, measure and learn. Exam angle: Beats big-bang launches.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Scaling AI

terms.definition: Pre-agreed measures that decide whether to scale. Exam angle: Set them before the pilot starts.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Scaling AI

terms.definition: Shared models, prompts, guardrails and data pipelines. Exam angle: Each new use case gets cheaper.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Scaling AI

terms.definition: Security, monitoring, support and SLAs in place. Exam angle: A pilot isn't production.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Scaling AI

terms.definition: How AI work is organized, funded and governed. Exam angle: Centralized, decentralized or hub-and-spoke.
terms.source_section: AIB-C01 / Domain 4: Readiness, leadership and transformation (24%) / Scaling AI

terms.definition: Central expertise hub plus embedded teams in business units. Exam angle: A common scaling pattern.

terms.definition: How to tell them apart: RAG adds knowledge at query time: current, cited, no retraining. Fine-tuning changes behavior or style and needs labeled data and retraining.
How to tell them apart: Always try prompting first. It's cheapest and fastest.
How to tell them apart: Training builds the model. Inference uses it, and that's the recurring production cost.
How to tell them apart: A number or category from history = predictive. New content = generative.
How to tell them apart: Known, stable, exact, auditable logic = rules.
How to tell them apart: A PoC proves it can work. A pilot proves it delivers value with real users.
How to tell them apart: Precision = few false alarms. Recall = few misses. Accuracy misleads on rare events.
How to tell them apart: Inputs change vs the input-to-outcome relationship changes.
How to tell them apart: Made-up facts vs systematic unfairness.
How to tell them apart: Why this output vs being open that and how AI is used.
How to tell them apart: Where data sits vs whose laws apply.
How to tell them apart: Accountable decision-maker vs day-to-day quality care.
How to tell them apart: Approves before action vs monitors and can intervene.
How to tell them apart: Better at the current role vs prepared for a different role.
How to tell them apart: Differentiator + data + skills = build. Commodity need = buy. Skill gap or speed = partner.
How to tell them apart: Variable demand vs steady high volume with committed capacity.
How to tell them apart: Not urgent and cheaper vs needs an instant answer.
How to tell them apart: Cost scales with use vs cost scales with users.
How to tell them apart: Use and adapt foundation models, managed vs build, train and deploy custom ML with full control.
How to tell them apart: Platform for builders vs ready-to-use AI workspace for business users.
How to tell them apart: Adoption and usage now vs financial results later.
How to tell them apart: Cash leaves the budget vs time is freed (only valuable if redeployed).
How to tell them apart: Enables and standardizes delivery vs approves and oversees risk.
How to tell them apart: An agent plans and acts with tools. A chatbot answers.
How to tell them apart: AWS secures the platform. You own your data, access, prompts, outputs and use-case choices.
